title: Selectivity of 2J2V for BET proteins in A549 cells
projectDescription: Data independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry was used to study the selectivity of 2J2V for BET proteins from A549 cells. BET proteins, BRD2, BRD3 and BRD4 were observed to be degraded the most by 2J2V in comparison to MZ1 or DMSO.
sampleProcessingProtocol: A549 cells treated with DSMSO, MZ1 and 2J2V in triplicate were decellularized and the protein extracts were reduced and alkylated. The proteins were then digested with Trypsin/Lys-C in S-trap microcolumn. The digested peptides were desalted and then injected to FAIMS embedded nano LC Orbitrap Lumos Fusion system.  The peptides were separated with mobile phase buffer A (0.1% formic acid) and B (acetonitrile/water (95:5(v/v)), over a 120-minute gradient (5–21% B in 62 minutes, 21-36% B in 48 minutes, 36-100% in 5 minutes and held at 100% B for 5 minutes). FAIMS compensation voltages were set to be -50 V and -70 V. Data acquisition was performed with DIA mode, in which each cycle of full scan of 395-1000 m/z at a resolution of 120,000 was performed. DIA MS2 scans at a resolution of 30,000 were performed for all DIA scans with 30 variable windows overlapped by 1 m/z. DIA spectra of both FAIMS compensation voltages were acquired.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry raw data were processed by Spectronaut software (version 16.2) using directDIA+ workflow with a FASTA database containing human reviewed sequences along with their isoforms of UniprotKB release of 2022_01. Carbamidomethyl (C) as fixed modification and M oxidation and N-terminal protein acetylation were set as variable modification. A maximum of two missed cleavages was allowed and false discovery rate was set at 1%. Precursors were filtered with q value and quantitation was done at MS2 level based on peak areas. Statistical analyses were done with Perseus (version 1.6.14.0) based on MS2 quantification data. Welch's T test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR of 0.05 was used to identify statistically significant proteins from the comparisons.
